item.title: Residence permit B in Fribourg: requirements, renewal & procedures
item.description: Practical guide to the requirements for obtaining and renewing the B permit in the Canton of Fribourg, with the necessary documents and procedure.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - Permit B is a renewable residence authorization for non-EU/EFTA workers with stable contracts (permanent or ≥12 months). In Canton Fribourg, 40% of annual applications concern this permit. - **Key requirements**: Valid job offer (salary compliant with sectoral standards), LAMal insurance (average cost: CHF 350/month), housing with minimum area of 20 m²/person. - Annual renewal tied to continuous employment and integration (language level A2 in French/German after 3 years). - Competent authority: Service de la population et des migrants (SPM) in Fribourg, with average processing times of 6 weeks (priority for critical sectors like healthcare and engineering).
## Key Facts Permit type: B (residence, annually renewable) Initial validity: 1 year (extendable to 2 years from the 2nd renewal) Renewal: Subject to active contract and absence of criminal convictions Essential documents: Passport, employment contract (≥CHF 60,000/year for qualified professions), LAMal proof, rental contract Competent office: Service de la population et des migrants (Rue des Chanoines 16, 1700 Fribourg) Reference law: Federal Act on Foreigners (LStr, last revised 2019) and Cantonal Integration Ordinance (2021).
Permit B in Canton Fribourg regulates residence for non-EU/EFTA citizens with subordinate contracts. The procedure requires employer involvement, who must demonstrate unavailability of local candidates (proof via 28-day advertisement on approved platforms like jobup.ch). In 2023, 65% of approved applications were in STEM and healthcare sectors.
### Fundamental Requirements 1. Concrete job offer: Contract with salary at least equal to the cantonal median for the profession (e.g.: CHF 85,000/year for an engineer, CHF 52,000 for a chef). Canton Fribourg applies salary checks via the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate Office. 2. Health insurance: Mandatory within 3 months (fine up to CHF 500 for delays). Companies like CSS or Helsana offer basic packages from CHF 280/month. 3. Adequate housing: In Fribourg city, average studio rent: CHF 1,200/month. Hygienic-sanitary compliance certification required (Art. 7 Cantonal Housing Act). 4. Integration: After 3 years, language test (e.g. telc A2 French certificate, cost CHF 200). Exemptions for over-55s or disabled persons.
> '30% of rejections stem from non-compliant housing or insufficient salaries' (SPM Report 2023).
### Operational Procedure The employer initiates the application online at *e-permis.fr.ch*, attaching: - Completed SPM-101 form - Passport copy and tourist permit (if applicable) - Detailed employment contract (hours, duties, salary) - Criminal record extract (<3 months) from country of origin and Switzerland - Housing proof (contract + floor plan)
Costs: CHF 150 (initial application) + CHF 100 (residence card). Processing time: 4-8 weeks (priority sectors: 3 weeks).
### Renewal and Practical Scenarios Case 1 (approved renewal): IT engineer with A2 in French and salary CHF 92,000 → 3-year renewal. Case 2 (refusal): Waiter without language certificate after 4 years → permit not renewed (Art. 63 LStr).
⚠️ Warning: Job loss > 6 months = permit revocation. Possible conversion to permit L (short-term) if new offer within 3 months.
💡 Tip: Annually verify salary standards on *salaires.fr.ch*. For housing, prioritize municipalities with vacancy rates >5% (e.g. Bulle or Villars-sur-Glâne). ## Practical Implications for Residents The Permit B offers stability but requires attention to annual deadlines. During the first year, the holder must: - Register with the commune of residence within 14 days of arrival (non-compliance: fine up to CHF 100, as per the Migration Act of Canton Fribourg, art. 12). - Obtain the legitimation certificate (biometric permit) within 30 days of registration. - Take out basic LAMal health insurance within 3 months: average premiums in Canton Fribourg in 2024 are CHF 450 monthly for an adult. Cantonal subsidies cover up to 60% for incomes below CHF 48,000 annually (example: family with 2 children and income of CHF 50,000 receives subsidies for CHF 28,800 annually).
### Renewal: What Changes After the First Year Renewal is not automatic. The office evaluates: 1. **Continuation of employment**: Written confirmation from the employer, indicating salary and contract duration. 2. Integration: Language proficiency (French/German). Fribourg assesses integration holistically, unlike Zurich or Basel-Country, which require A2 certificates (e.g., telc Suisse or Goethe-Institut). 3. Criminal record: No convictions for serious offenses (including abroad, per the Federal Act on Foreign Nationals, LEtr, art. 62b). 4. Tax compliance: Regular payment of federal taxes (average 8.5%), cantonal taxes (Fribourg: 6.3%), and communal taxes (example: Villars-sur-Glâne: 1.85%).
💡 Risk Scenarios: Job loss during the permit period allows 3–6 months to find new employment (Fribourg grants 6 months vs. 3 months in Geneva). In case of prolonged unemployment, the permit may be revoked (art. 63 LEtr). After 5 years of Permit B, you may apply for Permit C (permanent), reducing risks.
### Comparison with Other Cantons Renewal procedures in Canton Fribourg follow federal guidelines (Admission Ordinance, art. 17) but with cantonal discretion. Examples: - Language certificates: Explicitly required by Vaud (A2) and Bern (B1 for qualified jobs), while Fribourg assesses informal conversations during interviews. - Renewal times: 6–10 weeks in Fribourg vs. 8–12 weeks in Lausanne or 4–6 weeks in Bern. - Integration: Fribourg recognizes volunteer activities (e.g., 50 annual hours in local associations) as proof of integration, unlike Zurich, which prioritizes formal courses.
> 'Integration is not measured solely by a language test, but by participation in community life' (Director of the Fribourg Migration Office, 2023).
⚠️ Warning: Delays in renewal (beyond 90 days from expiry) may trigger expulsion procedures. Submit applications 3 months before expiry.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Concrete Actions for Applicants
### Step-by-step Procedure 1. **Document Preparation**: Valid passport (at least 6 months remaining validity), employment contract with a compliant minimum salary (e.g., CHF 4,500 gross/month for qualified individuals in Fribourg, according to the Admission Ordinance 2023), proof of accommodation (rental contract in municipalities like Bulle or Villars-sur-Glâne), criminal record certificate from the country of origin (apostilled if non-EU). 2. Employer's Application: The employer submits the application to the Cantonal Migration Office (in Fribourg: Chemin des Alpilles 34) with official form L, salary documentation (last 3 payslips), and proof of a 'labour market test' (demonstrates inability to hire Swiss/EU citizens). Cost: CHF 200. 3. Interview (if applicable): The office summons 15% of applicants (SEM 2024 data) to verify language skills (minimum B1 French) or job consistency. More frequent in sectors like construction (30% in Lausanne) compared to IT (5% in Zurich). 4. Decision: Written notification within 8-12 weeks (cantonal average). In case of refusal (e.g., insufficient salary or missing documents), written justification with reference to the Foreign Nationals Act (LEtr). 5. Permit Collection: After approval, book an appointment at the municipality (e.g., Fribourg city: within 10 days) for biometrics. Permit cost: CHF 150 (renewal CHF 100).
### Critical Deadlines - Renewal: Submit application at least 2 months in advance (e.g., expiry 31/10 → submission by 31/08). In 2023, 12% of late applications in Vaud experienced delays. - Employer Changes: Notify the cantonal office within 14 days (fine up to CHF 5,000 for delays, Art. 102 LStr). - Relocations: Report new address to the municipality within 8 days (in 2023, 20% of residents in Basel City received notices).
⚠️ Warning: Renewal delays can block international travel. The Fribourg Migration Office only accepts forms in French/German; certified translation services cost CHF 0.30/word.
> '40% of rejections stem from incomplete documentation. Double-check three times before submitting' (SEM Report 2024).
Operational Checklist: - [ ] Certified copy of passport (pp. 2-3) - [ ] Employment contract indicating LPP (occupational pension) and benefits - [ ] Bank statement as proof of funds (minimum CHF 20,000 for singles) - [ ] Health insurance compliant with LAMal (Swiss Health Insurance Act)
Scenario Comparison: A nurse in Fribourg (shortage sector) obtains a permit in 6 weeks; a bartender in Montreux (saturated quota) waits 4 months. Priority is given to professions on the SEM list (e.g., engineers, doctors).

item.title: Driving licence Zug: foreign conversion, exams & procedures
item.description: Complete guide to converting a foreign driver's license in the canton of Zug: required documents, theoretical and practical exams, mandatory courses and deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
## In short
 - Canton of Zug requires residents to convert foreign driving licences within 1 year
 - Theoretical (multilingual) and practical exam required, with some exceptions
 - Mandatory courses: first aid (10 hours) and ecological training (4 hours)
 - The Zug Road Traffic Office is the competent body

 ## Key Facts
 **Conversion deadline**: 1 year from the B/C permit
 Required exams: Theoretical + Practical
 Mandatory courses: First aid (10h) + Ecology (4h)
 Responsible office: Strassenverkehrsamt Zug
 Basic documents: Passport, permit, criminal record, photo

 For residents of the Canton of Zug with a foreign driving license, converting to a Swiss license is mandatory within one year of obtaining a B or C permit. The process involves the Strassenverkehrsamt Zug (Road Traffic Office), which verifies documents and administers exams. Candidates must pass both the theory and practical exams, except in specific cases. The theory exam can be taken in German, French, Italian, or English, reflecting Switzerland’s multilingual nature. The practical test evaluates driving skills in real-world conditions, with particular attention to safety and local regulations.

 ### Required documents
 The application requires a valid passport, B/C residence permit, criminal record from the country of origin (no older than 6 months), passport photo, and original driver’s license. The office verifies the authenticity and validity of these documents before admitting applicants to the exams.

 ### Courses ## Practical implications for residents
 Driving license conversion in the Canton of Zug is unique compared to other Swiss cantons. While some cantons recognize EU driving licenses without an exam, Zug maintains stringent requirements to ensure high road safety standards. This choice reflects the canton’s cautious approach, known for its low accident statistics (according to **FSO/BFS** data).

 ### Intercantonal comparison
 Unlike cantons like Vaud or Geneva, where EU citizens can exchange their driving license without an exam, Zug requires theory and practical tests for all non-Swiss drivers. This uniform policy simplifies administration but requires greater preparation from applicants. Mandatory courses, aligned with federal regulations on road safety, prepare drivers for the specific conditions of Switzerland, such as mountain roads and winter climates.

 ### Concrete scenarios
 Consider an Italian resident with a B permit: they must present their Italian criminal record, apostilled and translated. A candidate who already holds a Swiss license for another category (e.g., motorcycle) may be exempted from the practical car exam, at the office’s discretion. If they fail the theory exam, they can retake it after 14 days, while for the practical exam, the deadline is 30 days.

 The obligation to convert within 1 year avoids legal complications: driving with a foreign license after the deadline exposes
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## Step-by-step procedure
 1. **Document collection**: Obtain a criminal record and translate it into German (the official language of the canton).
 2. Course registration: Attend first aid (10h) and ecology (4h) at authorized centers.
 3. Official application: Send the form to the Strassenverkehrsamt Zug with all the documentation.
 4. Exam booking: Theoretical (at approved centres) and practical (with local instructor).

item.title: Mortgage rates in Switzerland: 10 years exceeds 2%
item.description: In September, 10-year mortgage rates rose to 2.06% and 5-year rates to 1.83%. End of the era of very low rates for the real estate market.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 10-year mortgage rates rose to 2.06% in September - 5-year mortgage rates increased to 1.83% - End of the ultra-low interest rate period in Switzerland - Upward pressure driven by international inflation
## Key Facts - 10-year mortgage rate: 2.06% - 5-year mortgage rate: 1.83% - Best 10-year rate: 1.60% - Best 5-year rate: 1.42% - Reference institution: SNB - Data source: Moneypark and Helvetia
Zurich recorded an increase in mortgage rates in September compared to June data. According to a survey conducted by Moneypark and Helvetia, reference rates for 5-year mortgages rose by 14 basis points, reaching 1.83%, while for 10-year terms, the increase was 8 basis points, bringing the value to 2.06%.
### Market Rate Details Even the best rates, accessible to clients with high creditworthiness and negotiating power, have seen an increase. Specifically, the most advantageous values now stand at 1.42% for 5-year mortgages and 1.60% for 10-year mortgages. Although rates have moved within a relatively narrow range since June, recent movements indicate that capital market dynamics and international inflation expectations are directly influencing the Swiss market.
Mortgage lenders expect upward pressure to continue, especially for long-term contracts. This scenario marks a clear departure from the period characterized by extremely low rates. While increases abroad have been more marked, the situation in Switzerland has remained more stable thanks to two main factors: moderate inflation and the strength of the Swiss franc. These elements have limited the need for more drastic interventions by the SNB, slowing a further rapid increase in real estate credit costs. item.title: Practical guide to looking for a job in Aargau 2026
item.description: The 2026 Swiss market offers places in engineering, technology, healthcare and logistics; in Aargau taxation is on three levels and AVS/AI/IPG contributions amount to 5.3% for employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Swiss labour market offers opportunities in sectors such as engineering, technology, healthcare and logistics - In Aargau the tax system is tiered at the federal, cantonal and municipal levels - Health insurance LAMal is mandatory for all residents - Work permits include L (short‑term), B (residence), C (permanent residence) and G (cross‑border commuters)
## Key facts - Taxation: three tiers (federal + cantonal + municipal) - AVS/AI/IPG contributions: 5.3% for employees (10.6% total) - Maximum working hours: 45 hours per week (industry, offices, sales) - Minimum holidays: 4 weeks (5 for under 20) - Permit C requires 10 years of residence (5 for EU/AELS)
The Swiss labour market continues to evolve in 2026, with the canton of Aargau maintaining a significant role in the national economy. The job market in Switzerland is primarily focused on sectors such as engineering, technology, healthcare and logistics, offering opportunities for both Swiss workers and foreigners holding the necessary permits. In the canton of Aargau, with its capital Aarau, the tax system is structured in three tiers: federal, cantonal and municipal, with each municipality applying a specific multiplier to the cantonal rate.
### The tax system in Aargau The Swiss tax system, also applied in Aargau, provides for three levels of taxation: federal, cantonal and municipal. The Federal Council sets the federal direct tax (IFD), while each canton has its own laws and multipliers. Municipalities, in turn, apply a multiplier to the cantonal rate. This tripartite system creates significant geographic differentiation between the various Swiss regions, with Aargau presenting competitive rates compared to other cantons.
Mandatory social security contributions include AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% for employees (10.6% total with the employer), AD/AC at 1.1% up to the annual maximum, and LAINF/LAA between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. Regarding occupational pension, the LPP provides variable rates based on age, with percentages that progressively increase. ### Job opportunities in canton Aargau Canton Aargau offers a dynamic labour market with opportunities in different sectors. According to official data, the maximum working time is 45 hours/week for the industrial, office and sales sectors, and up to 50 hours for other sectors. Workers are entitled to a minimum of 4 weeks of holiday per year (5 for workers under 20), while maternity covers 14 weeks at 80% of salary (IPG) and paternity 2 weeks.
Access to the labour market for foreigners requires the appropriate permits. The L permit is for short periods (up to 1 year), the B permit is renewable, while the C permit, required for long-term residence, normally requires 10 years of residence (reduced to 5 for EU/EFTA citizens). Border workers obtain the G permit, specific for those who reside abroad but work in Switzerland.
### Economic and social aspects The cost of living in Switzerland remains one of the highest in Europe, with considerable differences between cantons. LAMal health insurance is mandatory for all residents and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival. Premiums are calculated on an individual basis and vary by region, with deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 for adults. Many cantons, including Aargau, offer subsidies to reduce the cost of premiums.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Practical procedure for job search in Switzerland For those seeking employment in Switzerland, including candidates for the canton of Aargau, it is essential to follow a structured procedure. It will start with preparing a curriculum vitae that meets Swiss standards, highlighting education, work experience, language skills and references. The CV should be written in at least two languages, preferably German and English for Aargau.
Job search can take place through various channels: specialized online portals, temporary employment agencies, job fairs and direct contacts with companies. It is important to note that Switzerland does not have a federal minimum wage, although some cantons have introduced specific minimum rates. The interested company will then start the procedures to obtain the necessary work permit for a candidate.
### Documents and deadlines The documents required to work in Switzerland include: passport or identity card, work or residence permit, social security number (AVS), proof of residence, and professional qualification documents. Regarding housing, federal law provides a maximum security deposit of three months' rent, to be paid into a blocked account in the tenant's name. The landlord's termination is valid only on an official cantonal form, and any disputes must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority.
For those moving to Switzerland, it is essential to take out LAMal health insurance within three months of arrival. Social security contributions are deducted directly from the salary, with rates varying by sector and age. item.title: Summer 2026: over 2 billion francs of lost productivity
item.description: Summer 2026 caused productivity losses of over CHF 2 billion, with Birsfelden at 2.47% and the affected cities at 1.3 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The 2026 summer caused productivity losses of 2 billion CHF - Calculations based on the ETH model and MeteoSwiss data - Smaller municipalities suffer the highest loss rates - Birsfelden (BL) records the peak with a 2.47% loss
## Key facts - Loss amount: over 2 billion francs - Affected cities: 1.3 billion francs - Ratio: 3.2 times higher than the average - Worst municipality: Birsfelden (2.47%) - Data source: MeteoSwiss - Institution: Swiss Cities Association
### The study's figures The 2026 heatwave had a profound impact on the Swiss economy, generating an estimated loss in labor productivity of over two billion francs. This figure emerges from calculations by the Swiss Cities Association, which are based on a model developed by the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich (ETH). The publication was previewed by the NZZ am Sonntag newspaper and subsequently confirmed by Keystone-ATS. The analysis considered the months from June to August, a period during which anomalous temperatures reduced worker performance across the country.
The mechanism is clear: intense heat alters sleep quality and increases the sensation of fatigue, slowing down work rhythms. These heat stress effects are considered established parameters in occupational medicine. To quantify the damage, researchers used temperature data provided by MeteoSwiss. The reference value for an average summer, according to the 2022 ETH study, is 665 million francs. However, the 2026 summer showed values approximately 3.2 times higher than this baseline, justifying the record figure of two billion francs.
### Cities under pressure Urban areas proved to be the most vulnerable. This is due to two reasons: the high concentration of economic strength and the intensity of temperatures. The 172 centers statistically defined as cities suffered a total productivity loss of 1.3 billion francs. Although the 15 largest cities recorded the highest absolute losses, the phenomenon disproportionately affected smaller municipalities located in agglomerations. The latter suffered the highest loss rates in percentage terms relative to their economic base. The most emblematic case is that of Birsfelden, in the canton of Basel-Country, which tops the rankings with a 2.47% loss in productivity.

item.title: The Federal Council improves the application of ISOs
item.description: Approve the changes to OISOS and OPT by the Federal Council to simplify and speed up building projects in Switzerland from 1 November 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Amendments approved on 18 September 2026 - New provisions in force from 1 November 2026 - Expected impact report by the end of 2028
## Key facts What: Edit OISOS and opt Date: September 18, 2026 Entry into force: 1 November 2026 Competence: Federal Department of the Interior
At its meeting on 18 September 2026, the Federal Council approved an amendment to the Ordinance on the Federal Inventory of Swiss Settlements to be Protected (OISOS) and the Ordinance on Spatial Planning (OPT). This decision makes it possible to clarify the application of the ISOs and to simplify and speed up the processing of numerous planning and construction projects throughout Switzerland. At the same time, the federal executive has adopted the latest updates of the ISOs in the Canton of Graubünden. With this intervention, the Federal Council offers a concrete response to the practical problems encountered so far in the application of the requirements regarding the protection of settlements. The new provisions aim to make planning and authorisation procedures simpler and faster, without disproportionately limiting the protection of cultural heritage and historic settlements. The executive highlighted how the primary objective is to remove bureaucratic obstacles that slowed down procedures in the Municipalities and Cantons.
### The path of public consultation The proposed changes to OISOS and OPT The amendments approved by the Federal Council respond to the fundamental need to reconcile the rigorous protection of historical settlements of national importance with the current challenges of urban and energy development. To date, the application of protection regulations often generated administrative delays and legal uncertainties in cantons and municipalities during the review of construction projects. With the revision of the ordinances, a better balance is established between the protection of cultural heritage, quality centripetal development, the urgent need to build new housing to meet housing demand, and the strategic objectives linked to the energy transition. This regulatory evolution offers real estate operators, designers, and local administrations clearer rules for managing urban densification projects and the energy retrofitting of existing buildings located within protected perimeters.
### Conclusion of the Update in the Grisons Concurrently with the revision of the general ordinances, the Federal Council has formally concluded the revision of the list of settlements of importance for the Canton of Grisons, which represents the largest canton in the Confederation. During the same session, the executive adopted the latest territorial modifications by officially including the settlements of Hinterrhein, Jenaz, and Vals-Platz, while the settlement of Roveredo was formally removed from the federal inventory. The new surveys regarding Hinterrhein, Jenaz, and Vals-Platz will enter into force on November 1, 2026. Starting from that date, all updated data will be accessible to the public and industry professionals in digital format, specifically as geodata and in PDF format, which can be consulted directly on the official geoportal of the Confederation (map.geo.admin.ch) and on the dedicated thematic portal (gisos.bak.admin.ch). ISOS thus continues to represent the fundamental reference tool for cantonal and municipal authorities responsible for the conservation of historical monuments, the protection of traditional buildings, and long-term spatial planning.

The operational phase following the approval of the amendments involves constant monitoring of the impact of the new rules in the field. The Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) has been tasked with monitoring and evaluating the actual impact of the provisions in the daily practice of local authorities and operators. By the end of 2028, the FDHA will present an official evaluation report to the Federal Council to verify whether the objectives of simplifying and accelerating procedures have been fully achieved without compromising the protection of Swiss architectural heritage. For planning professionals, municipalities, and property owners involved in construction projects in protected areas, the immediate deadlines concern the entry into force set for November 1, 2026, the date from which the new interest-weighting criteria and updated provisions for the Canton of Graubünden will apply.

item.title: Schengen Dublin Report: Impacts on GDP and Border
item.description: The Federal Council adopted the report on Schengen and Dublin: abandonment could reduce Swiss GDP by up to 3.9% in 2035.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Il Consiglio federale ha adottato il rapporto su Schengen/Dublino il 18 settembre 2026 - L'abbandono potrebbe ridurre il PIL svizzero fino al 3,9% nel 2035 - Perdita di reddito annua stimata fino a 1300 franchi pro capite - Benefici rilevanti per l'economia, il turismo, l'asilo e la sicurezza interna
## Fatti chiave Data rapporto: 18 settembre 2026 Pertinenza: Consiglio federale svizzero Impatto sul PIL nel 2035: Fino al 3,9 per cento Perdita di reddito pro capite: Fino a 1300 franchi all'anno Postulato di riferimento: Postulato 24.3946 del Gruppo liberale radicale RL
Il 18 settembre 2026, il Consiglio federale svizzero ha adottato un importante rapporto che analizza gli effetti economici, finanziari e sulla sicurezza di un eventuale abbandono degli accordi di Schengen e Dublino con l'Unione Europea. La Svizzera trae attualmente considerevoli vantaggi da questi accordi bilaterali, che garantiscono una circolazione transfrontaliera fluida per merci e persone, elementi fondamentali per preservare il benessere e l'attrattiva della piazza economica nazionale. Secondo lo studio esterno che fa da base al documento ufficiale redatto su incarico del Consiglio nazionale tramite il postulato del Gruppo liberale radicale RL, l'uscita da Schengen e Dublino avrebbe conseguenze estremamente pesanti per il Paese entro l'orizzonte temporale del 2035.
Il rapporto evidenzia come il prodotto interno lordo svizzero potrebbe subire una contrazione fino al 3,9 per cento nel 2035, mentre la perdita di reddito annua per ogni singolo cittadino ammonterebbe fino a 1300 franchi pro capite. Senza gli accordi vigenti, infatti, il diritto europeo imporrebbe ai Paesi confinanti di sottoporre a rigorosi controlli tutte le entrate e le uscite, trasformando il confine svizzero in una vera e propria frontiera esterna dello spazio Schengen. Di conseguenza, anche la Confederazione sarebbe costretta a potenziare in modo significativo le proprie infrastrutture doganali e il personale addetto ai controlli territoriali, generando una pesante interruzione nella catena logistica e di mobilità transfrontaliera.
### Scenari economici per il 2035 Le proiezioni economiche contenute nel documento indicano chiaramente che la mancanza di un accordo sulla libera circolazione influirebbe negativamente su molteplici settori chiave dell'economia nazionale. Tra questi figurano non solo l'industria e il commercio di merci, ma anche comparti strategici come il turismo e i servizi legati alla ristorazione e alle cure, che dipendono fortemente dalla rapidità degli spostamenti e dall'afflusso regolare di personale e visitatori internazionali. I risparmi derivanti dalla cessazione della cooperazione non coprirebbero in alcun modo i costi supplementari necessari per la gestione autonoma dei confini e per il mantenimento di standard di sicurezza adeguati, confermando che i benefici complessivi superano ampiamente gli aspetti meramente finanziari. ## Analysis of impacts on key sectors and the labor market
A potential breakdown of the Schengen and Dublin agreements would cause profound disruptions and critical issues in the Swiss labor market, directly hitting the cross-border workforce and companies operating in Switzerland. Without effective cross-border free movement, estimates for 2035 indicate that cross-border workers could lose a total of 422,000 hours on working days due to massive traffic congestion generated by the new and inevitable customs controls at the border crossings. This slowdown in daily mobility would generate annual costs estimated between 1.08 and 2.27 billion francs for the Swiss economy. The reintroduction of controls would also result in a drop in the number of cross-border workers of up to 60 percent, triggering severe staff shortages especially in the economic sectors of catering and care, where foreign labor plays a structural and irreplaceable role.
### Demographic and migratory dynamics Repercussions on the labor market would not stop at the decrease in commuting workers. Due to daily transit difficulties and bureaucratic barriers at the border, the probability that up to 170,000 people will decide to permanently transfer their residence to Switzerland would increase drastically, significantly altering the demographic fabric and pressure on the residential real estate market of the border cantons. To learn more about labor market trends and current professional opportunities, you can consult the dedicated page [job offers](nav:jobs) available on the portal.
### Effects on tourism and the asylum sector The tourism sector would suffer a heavy blow, since membership in Schengen currently allows travelers from third countries subject to visa requirements to move without barriers throughout the integrated area. In the absence of the agreement, tourists would face a considerable financial and administrative burden to obtain a separate Swiss visa. The study predicts a drop in demand and revenue in the Swiss tourism sector quantifiable between 320 and 810 million francs in 2035. Similarly, in the asylum sector, Switzerland would lose the procedural advantages of the Dublin system, finding itself obliged to examine applications from applicants who have already filed a claim in another participating State. The inability to carry out transfers to such States would prolong the stay of asylum seekers on Swiss territory, resulting in an increase in costs estimated between 166 and 824 million francs.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Internal security and judicial cooperation
Beyond purely economic and financial implications, the Federal Council report highlights the invaluable value of the Schengen and Dublin databases for safeguarding Switzerland's internal security. During 2025, solely thanks to the use of the Schengen Information System known as SIS, Swiss security authorities obtained nearly 40,000 relevant and targeted hits, especially regarding individuals flagged as dangerous or wanted for criminal activities. Switzerland would not have any autonomous or national measure capable of compensating for the loss of these shared databases and international police cooperation tools. The direct consequence would be the inability to timely or fully identify threats to public security, severely hindering the effectiveness of criminal prosecution and leaving the country exposed to high criminal risks.
### Operational dependence and financial sustainability Maintaining external borders and managing autonomous national databases would require colossal financial investments that could never be offset by savings resulting from a hypothetical withdrawal from the agreements. Furthermore, the effectiveness of border controls would depend to a large extent on the cooperation and human resources provided by neighboring countries and the European Union, effectively making Switzerland dependent on foreign decisions for the management of its territory and traffic flows. Customs queues would become all the longer and more paralyzing the fewer personnel were employed by neighboring countries at checkpoints.
### How to check your finances and cost of living Faced with complex macroeconomic scenarios that can directly influence purchasing power, net salary, and the financial stability of families living in Switzerland, it is essential to carefully monitor one's economic situation and the evolution of taxes and contributions. To accurately assess your payslip, understand the impact of social deductions, and better plan your financial and tax resources, you can use our official tool available on the salary calculator page [salary calculator](nav:calculator).

item.title: Lidl abolishes cash rounding for cards and online
item.description: German discount Lidl has eliminated downward rounding for card and online payments, saving over a million francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Elimination of rounding down on online and card payments - The new measure introduced by Lidl starting this spring - Rounding down remains in force for cash payments - Estimated savings for the discounter of over one million francs
## Key facts - Company: Lidl - Introduction period: Spring - Methods affected: Online and card payments - Method excluded: Cash payments - Estimated savings: Over one million francs - Competitor precedent: Aldi abolished the practice since last autumn
Large-scale retail giant Lidl has officially removed the custom of rounding down shopping amounts for those who choose to pay for their purchases using digital instruments or electronic money in Switzerland. The news, which emerged thanks to Sunday press publications with a report by the SonntagsBlick, reveals a radical change in the management of electronic payments within the stores of the German-origin discount chain on Swiss territory.
### The end of commercial courtesy Until recently, the commercial policy of the well-known chain included a very precise rule to accommodate customers: if the final sum of the receipt did not end with the digit zero or the number five, the system automatically provided for rounding down. This procedure resulted in a practical reduction of the total to be paid by the buyer. A clear example reported by the chronicles highlights how a total bill equal to forty-three francs and fifty-three cents was automatically lowered to forty-three francs and fifty cents, thus offering a small immediate economic advantage to the consumer during the payment of the shopping. ### Timing and impact of commercial innovation The evolution of the payment system is not a measure recently announced, but a structural change that has already been operational for several months. According to what emerges from the Sunday newspaper checks, the transition to the punctual calculation system would have been implemented indicatively starting from the spring of thisyear in the various points of sale of the distribution network. Anyone who spends forty-three francs and fifty-three cents today will be charged exactly one cent, without any reduction or cash favour, if they decide to use their credit or debit card or the online payment channels available online.
### Benchmarking with competitors in the market The decision taken by Lidl's top management does not represent an isolated episode in the retail and discount landscape operating in Switzerland. Already during the autumn of last year, another important player in the sector such as Aldi had taken steps to completely remove a similar commercial custom from its coffers. This strategic convergence between the main discount operators highlights a common trend aimed at the standardisation of accounting procedures and the millimetre management of financial flows deriving from daily retail sales in Italy.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Business reasons and industry standards When questioned on the matter by local newspapers, Lidl's management justified the elimination of this concession by directly referring to the current market standard. According to the official position expressed by the retail chain, adopting a rounding-free system for electronic payments guarantees a significantly higher level of transparency for customers. The formal reason lies in the possibility of always paying the exact amount down to the exact cent corresponding to the real monetary value of the items placed in the cart and purchased.
### Current cash management and corporate savings It should be emphasized that downward rounding remains fully in force exclusively for all customers who choose to make their payments in cash at the register. At the same time, the company reiterates that upward rounding is never permitted under the applied provisions. Regarding the financial aspect of the measure, the removal of this concession on digital payments proves to be an extremely advantageous operation for the group's accounts: already back in 2020, the company itself had calculated that the previously practiced rounding had resulted in foregoing over one million francs given away in total to customers over time. ## In brief - Migros is evaluating the merger of its 10 regional cooperatives - Variants are being studied: 3 cooperatives or 1 single entity - 2.3 million members could be consulted - No decision has been made yet; Vision 2035 strategy
## Key facts - **Who**: Migros, Mario Irminger (CEO) - What: Restructuring of regional cooperatives - Number of members: 2.3 million - Source: NZZ am Sonntag - Strategy: Vision 2035 - Status: Under evaluation, no decision made
### A historic turning point for the orange giant Zurich is witnessing a potential paradigm shift in the structure of one of Switzerland's largest companies. According to reports by 'NZZ am Sonntag', Migros is evaluating a deep restructuring that could lead to the merger of its ten regional cooperatives. The most radical hypothesis, which CEO Mario Irminger would prefer, is the creation of a single cooperative for the entire country. However, no definitive decision has been made yet, although an agreement between the parties is reportedly not far off.
The current organizational structure dates back to 1941, when founder Gottlieb Duttweiler consciously chose to create strong regions and a weaker central body. This model, which has remained unchanged for over 80 years, is today considered obsolete by many industry observers. The reasons for the possible reform are operational in nature: the current system involves duplicated structures and lengthy decision-making processes, which slow down the company's responsiveness in an increasingly competitive market.

## In breve - Oltre 125'000 firme raccolte in 3 mesi - Referendum contro nuove centrali nucleari - Possibile voto il 28 febbraio 2027
## Fatti chiave - Numero firme: 125'000 - Periodo raccolta: 3 mesi - Data consegna firme: 6 ottobre - Data ipotetica voto: 28 febbraio 2027 - Progetto controprogetto: revoca divieto nuove centrali - Coalizione: Verdi, PS, PVL, parte del Centro, ATA, WWF, Greenpeace, Pro Natura, Swissolar
Il comitato referendario ha annunciato questa sera, confermando un’informazione già pubblicata sul sito del Tages Anzeiger, che sono state raccolte più di 125 000 firme in soli tre mesi per avviare un referendum contro la costruzione di nuove centrali nucleari in Svizzera. La raccolta è stata definita “un segnale chiaro del rifiuto popolare al ritorno del nucleare”, secondo il comunicato della coalizione «No alle nuove centrali nucleari». Il documento sottolinea che la tecnologia nucleare è “costosa e pericolosa” e aumenta la dipendenza dalla Russia per l’uranio.
### Dettagli della raccolta firme Il comitato ha precisato che le firme saranno consegnate alla Cancelleria federale il 6 ottobre. Se la raccolta verrà dichiarata valida, gli aventi diritto di voto potranno esprimersi sulla modifica legislativa già prevista per il 28 febbraio 2027. La coalizione ricorda che, nella sessione estiva, le Camere federali hanno approvato il controprogetto indiretto del Consiglio federale all’iniziativa popolare “Energia elettrica in ogni tempo per tutti (Stop al blackout)”, che prevede la revoca del divieto di costruire nuove centrali nucleari. La coalizione accusa il Consiglio federale e il Parlamento di “ignorare la volontà popolare”.
Il comitato richiama inoltre tre precedenti decisioni popolari a favore delle energie rinnovabili: l’adozione della Strategia energetica 2050 nel 2017, la legge sulla protezione del clima nel 2023 e la legge sull’elettricità nel 2024. Secondo i promotori, la Svizzera sta già coprendo una quota crescente del fabbisogno energetico con solare, eolico e idroelettrico locali, mentre i costi e i rischi del nucleare sono considerati “troppo elevati”. La coalizione è composta da partiti verdi e di centro‑sinistra, oltre a una trentina di organizzazioni ambientaliste, tra cui l’Associazione traffico e ambiente (ATA), il WWF, Greenpeace, Pro Natura e Swissolar. The practical consequences of a successful referendum result are relevant for all Swiss citizens and businesses. If the legislative amendment is approved, Switzerland will have to remain faithful to the ban on building new nuclear power plants, consolidating its dependence on renewable sources such as solar, wind and hydroelectric. This entails a strengthening of investments in grid infrastructure to manage the variability of renewable production, with potential impacts on electricity costs for households and businesses.
### Comparison with the current situation Currently, the Federal Council has already initiated a counter-project that revokes the ban, opening the door to new nuclear construction. A vote in favour of the referendum would mean a reversal: Switzerland will return to a policy of shutting down nuclear power, as set out in the Energy Strategy 2050 and recent laws on climate protection and electricity. In practice, companies will have to adapt investment plans, giving up any nuclear projects and focusing on renewable sources. Cantonal authorities, which manage incentives for green energy, could see higher demand for contributions and permits for solar and wind plants.
### Possible scenarios - **Scenario A – Approved Referendum:** Ban remains; uranium imports, particularly from Russia, will not increase.

## In brief - Votes in nine Cantons on Sunday, September 27 - Themes: taxation, civil rights, education, and mobility - Focus on tax cuts in Vaud and the vote on 16-year-olds' voting rights in Graubünden - Investments for cross-border mobility in Geneva
## Key facts Date: September 27 Locations: Nine Cantons Geneva mobility credit: 39.5 million Swiss francs Geneva traffic target: -15,000 vehicles per day
On Sunday, September 27, voters in nine Swiss Cantons will be called to the polls to decide on a series of reforms affecting the economy, civil rights, and social policies. The consultations cover a wide spectrum of topics, ranging from land use planning to education, including issues related to contraception, hooliganism, and infrastructure for cross-border mobility.
### The main cantonal consultations Among the most relevant themes are the initiative for a substantial reduction in taxes in the Canton of Vaud and the proposal to extend the right to vote to 16-year-olds in the Canton of Graubünden. In Basel-Country, the vote will concern the law on compensation for capital gains from land use planning, following a Federal Court ruling that found part of the current regulation non-compliant. In this case, voters will have to choose between an initiative by the Association of Landowners (HEV), which aims for minimal contributions and strict limits on the use of funds, and a counter-proposal by the Grand Council that provides for slightly higher contributions.
In the Canton of Basel-City, the SVP (Swiss People's Party) has launched the 'anti-chaos' initiative, which aims to make participants in unauthorized demonstrations responsible for police costs and damages caused. The proposal includes extending such liability to those who resort to violence during authorized gatherings and asks the Government for a plan to reduce unauthorized demonstrations. In parallel, citizens of Basel-City will vote on an initiative to use a trade fair pavilion as a storage facility for the Historical Museum, the State Archives, and the University Library, to avoid new constructions near the University.
In the Canton of Bern, attention is focused on education. A popular initiative requests that the right to quality education be enshrined in the cantonal constitution, obliging the Canton and Municipalities to guarantee high-level teaching and qualified staff throughout the territory. Calculate your taxes to understand the impact of potential tax reforms in the different Cantons. ### Analysis of Tax and Social Reforms The votes scheduled for September 27th reveal a divergence in approaches among the various Cantons, particularly regarding the management of public finances and social services. In the Canton of Vaud, the call for a substantial tax reduction represents an attempt to lighten the tax burden on taxpayers, a theme with direct implications for the purchasing power of residents. This contrasts with the situation in Basel-Country, where the debate shifts to the redistribution of land-use planning surpluses, highlighting the tension between the interests of landowners (HEV) and the funding needs of municipalities.
On the front of civil rights and health, the Socialist Party's (PS) initiative in Geneva for free contraception raises questions about equity in access to sexual health. While the left and the Centre support the text, the Council of State, along with the PLR, MCG, and UDC, contests the proposal, deeming it not sufficiently targeted at lower-income brackets and potentially costly. This debate reflects the complexity of implementing social subsidies in a system where the efficiency of public spending is constantly monitored.
### Impact on Mobility and Infrastructure A case of particular relevance for those commuting between Switzerland and France is the proposed credit of 39.5 million francs in Geneva. The investment is intended to co-finance infrastructure in French territory, including 1,600 new parking spaces in P+R facilities, bus priority lanes, and the expansion of the tram network. The operational goal is to reduce daily traffic by 15,000 vehicles on the roads of the Canton. This project demonstrates how traffic management and pollution require coordinated cross-border solutions to improve urban quality of life.
For those residing in Switzerland, these changes directly influence the cost of living and the efficiency of public services. Smoother mobility in Geneva could reduce travel times, while decisions on education in Bern or voting rights in the Grisons redefine the social contract at the local level. It is possible to monitor price trends and the impact of these measures by consulting the data on the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living).

Voters will receive the informational material and ballot papers at their home address. It is fundamental to carefully read the differences between the popular initiative and any potential counter-proposal, as in the case of Basel-Country, where the option proposed by the Grand Council differs in the amount of contributions requested compared to the proposal by the HEV.
For those interested in tax reforms, especially in the Canton of Vaud, it is advisable to analyze their current tax situation. Since the Swiss tax system is structured on three levels (federal, cantonal, and municipal), a reduction in cantonal taxes can significantly vary the net annual amount depending on the municipal multiplier applied. Those wishing to plan their budget in view of potential tax changes can use simulation tools to forecast the actual savings.

Consult the voting booklet to understand the implications of the 39.5 million franc credit for mobility in Geneva, if you reside or work in that area. 3. Evaluate the impact of the proposals on education or health (free contraception) based on your family and income profile. 4. Monitor the decisions of the Federal Court that have led to new votes, as happened with land planning in Basel-Country.
The analysis of these votes allows understanding how cantonal policies influence not only the tax burden but also access to essential services and land management. ## In a nutshell - **Revolut**, an online bank, suffered a hack that led to the delivery of data of almost 700 customers to cybercriminals. - Hackers posed as Italian authorities, putting pressure on Revolut. - No money was stolen, but sensitive data such as passport information and account numbers. - The incident mainly involves Swiss customers.
## Key facts - Hacker attack: Revolut provided data to cybercriminals. - Method: Hackers exploited an official Italian communication channel (PEC). - Compromised data: Passports, accounts and addresses of almost 700 customers. - Victims: especially Swiss customers. - Ransom: Hackers demand $3 million from Revolut not to publish the data.
The hacker attack on the online bank Revolut also affected Switzerland, involving a significant number of Swiss customers. The hackers acted in an unusual way, publishing their ransom demand on a website and addressing public opinion instead of negotiating directly with the company. This has raised questions about the real motivations of cybercriminals.
> "Normally hackers negotiate privately directly with their victims," explains Pascal Lago, SRF's economic editor. "Criminals then turn to public opinion rather than directly to the affected company. This raises a lot of questions, for example whether it is really just about money or whether the The hacker attack on Revolut raises concerns about the security of Swiss customers' personal data. The incident highlights the vulnerability of official communication channels, such as the Italian PEC, which can be exploited by cybercriminals to obtain sensitive information. This case highlights the need to strengthen security measures and raise users' awareness of the importance of protecting their personal data.
> "For this reason there is great nervousness in Italy," says Pascal Lago. "Hackers could also access the data of many other companies. For this reason, the Italian authorities are also investigating the case. "
The impact on Revolut's image in Switzerland could be significant, especially considering the recent banking license application. Swiss customers, who often use Revolut as an additional account for holidays abroad, may be discouraged by the incident and prefer other safer options. In addition, the incident could have repercussions on the trust of customers towards online banks in general, pushing them to prefer traditional institutions with physical branches.

## Key facts Apprenticeship contract: Mandatory Apprentice remuneration: Variable by sector and year Vocational maturity: Possible for many apprentices Apprenticeship duration: Varies according to profession
In the Canton of Vaud, the apprenticeship and vocational training pathway represents a privileged route for entering the labour market, offering young people practical skills and a solid foundation for their future career. Searching for an apprenticeship position requires a targeted approach that takes into account the specificities of the canton and the various professions available. The apprenticeship contract, a fundamental document that regulates the relationship between apprentice, employer and vocational school, must be signed before the start of training. This contract defines crucial aspects such as the duration of the apprenticeship, training objectives, working hours, remuneration and holidays.
The remuneration of an apprentice in the Canton of Vaud, as in the rest of Switzerland, is not set at federal level and varies significantly according to the professional sector, the year of training and the company’s wage policy. Generally, the salary increases progressively throughout the apprenticeship years. It is essential to inquire about average wages for the desired profession by consulting cantonal professional associations or dedicated vocational training guides. In addition to on‑the‑job training, the apprentice attends a vocational school where they acquire the necessary theoretical knowledge. For many professions, it is also possible to obtain the vocational maturity certificate, a qualification that opens the door to higher education at the Universities of Applied Sciences and Arts (UAS), further broadening career prospects. Admission procedures for the vocational maturity certificate vary, but often require passing specific exams at the end of the apprenticeship. The cantonal authorities of Vaud, through their vocational training offices, provide support and detailed information to guide young people and companies through this essential training pathway. ### Finding the ideal internship position The search for an internship position in the Canton of Vaud takes place through various channels. Cantonal professional associations and chambers of commerce play a central role, often publishing internship offers on their online portals or organizing fairs dedicated to vocational training. Vocational schools themselves also provide active support in the search, making available information about partner companies and available positions. It is advisable to start the search well in advance, usually a year before the expected start of the internship, as the most sought-after applications are often filled quickly. Preparing a complete and personalized application dossier, which includes a detailed curriculum vitae and a convincing motivation letter, is essential to stand out. An orientation interview or a trial period in a company can represent further steps in the selection process, allowing both the candidate and the employer to assess mutual suitability.
### The internship contract and remuneration Once the desired position has been identified, signing the internship contract is the next step. This legal document, drafted according to cantonal and federal directives, establishes the rights and duties of all parties involved. It must clearly state the profession of the internship, the total duration, the start and end dates, the workplace, the weekly working hours, the annual leave (which cannot be less than that provided for by the federal labour law, i.e. four weeks for adults and five for those under 20 years of age), the monthly remuneration and the payment terms. The remuneration of an apprentice in the Canton of Vaud, as mentioned, is highly variable. To give an idea, the first years of apprenticeship can foresee salaries ranging from a few hundred to over one thousand Swiss francs per month, with significant increases in the following years. The exact figures depend heavily on the sector (for example, an apprentice in an industrial sector may earn a different remuneration from one in a commercial office or a shop). It is always advisable to consult the indicative salary tables provided by the trade associations to obtain a more precise picture.

item.title: Permit L Graubünden: validity and extension
item.description: The L permit for Grisons is valid for up to 1 year, with the possibility of extension and transfer to B permit under specific conditions and constraints for the employer.

## In brief - L permit for Graubünden: validity up to 1 year. - Extension possible, but with limits. - Transition to B permit to be evaluated. - Constraints for the employer.
## Key facts Short-term permit: L Maximum duration: 1 year Extension: possible Transition to B permit: possible Employer requirements: yes
The short-term work permit, known as the L permit, is a type of residency authorization for foreign workers who intend to carry out gainful employment in Switzerland for a limited period, usually not exceeding one year. In the canton of Graubünden, as in the rest of the Confederation, the L permit is subject to specific regulations that define its duration, the conditions for extension, and the requirements for its possible renewal or transformation into a residence permit (B permit). Its issuance is strictly linked to a concrete job offer and to certain conditions that must be met by both the employee and the employer. The main objective of this permit is to facilitate the entry of foreign labour for temporary labour needs, without however creating an automatic right to long-term residence in the country. It is essential to understand that the L permit is not, by itself, indefinitely renewable; its nature is intrinsically temporary. The cantonal authorities of Graubünden, within their competence, carefully assess each individual application, taking into account factors such as the local labour market situation and the professional qualifications of the applicant. The expiry of the L permit obliges the holder to leave Swiss territory, unless the requirements for an extension or for the issuance of another type of permit are met. Procedures and requirements may vary slightly depending on the sector of activity and the nationality of the applicant, but the general principle of temporal limitation remains unchanged. Strict compliance with current regulations is essential to avoid future complications and to ensure the legality of the stay in Switzerland. Its validity is strictly tied to the duration of the employment contract or to the specific reason for which it was granted, and its expiry does not confer the right to remain in Swiss territory without further authorisation. The competent authorities of Graubünden are responsible for verifying the fulfilment of the requirements and deciding on the possible granting of extensions or transformations, always in compliance with federal legislation on foreigners and labour. The temporary nature of the L permit requires careful planning on the part of the foreign worker and his/her future employer, considering the long-term implications of staying in Switzerland. The management of the L permit in the Canton of Graubünden requires a careful assessment of the possibilities for extension and, in some cases, of transition to a residence permit (permit B). Although the L permit is intended for short-term stays, Swiss law allows, in specific and justified circumstances, its extension. However, it is crucial to understand that extensions are not automatic and are subject to an evaluation by the competent cantonal authorities. These authorities will verify whether the conditions that led to the initial issuance of the L permit still exist and whether there are new elements justifying an extension of the work stay. A fundamental aspect to consider is the link with the employer. Often, the extension of the L permit is conditional on the continuation of the employment relationship with the same company or on a new job that meets the requirements for this type of permit. In the absence of a valid job offer or if work needs cease, the extension is unlikely to be granted. For those who intend to settle more permanently in the Canton of Graubünden, the possibility of moving from an L permit to a B permit (residence) represents an option to consider. This transition entails a new application procedure and the demonstration of meeting more stringent requirements, such as the ability to support oneself economically independently and, for citizens of certain third countries, the absence of threats to security and public order. The change from L to B is not an automatic right and depends on the discretionary evaluation of the authorities, who will consider the individual situation of the applicant and the needs of the local labor market. It is important to emphasize that the application for conversion must be submitted before the expiration of the current L permit. Ignoring deadlines or failing to follow procedures may result in the need to leave Swiss territory. Consultation with the competent cantonal offices or with professionals experienced in foreign nationals' law is strongly recommended to navigate these procedures correctly and to plan as best as possible one's future work and stay in Switzerland, especially in a specific cantonal context like that of Graubünden, which may have administrative peculiarities linked to its size and economic structure.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). La gestione del permesso L nel Cantone dei Grigioni implica una serie di passaggi pratici e adempimenti burocratici sia per il lavoratore straniero che per il datore di lavoro. Una volta ottenuto il permesso L, la sua validità è strettamente legata alla durata del contratto di lavoro sottoscritto. È essenziale che sia il lavoratore che il datore di lavoro ne monitorino attentamente la scadenza per evitare situazioni di irregolarità. Qualora si desideri prolungare il soggiorno oltre la durata originaria del permesso L, è necessario presentare una richiesta di proroga alle autorità cantonali competenti con un congruo anticipo rispetto alla data di scadenza. La documentazione richiesta per la proroga solitamente include una nuova offerta di lavoro o una conferma della continuazione del rapporto lavorativo, oltre a eventuali altri documenti che le autorità potrebbero richiedere per valutare la sussistenza dei presupposti per l'estensione. Se l'obiettivo a lungo termine è stabilirsi in modo più permanente nei Grigioni, è opportuno informarsi sulla possibilità di richiedere un permesso di dimora (permesso B). ## Key facts Scope: Compulsory schooling Location: Canton of Vaud Elements: Cycles, enrollment, calendar, languages Objective: Transition to upper secondary schools
The school system of the Canton of Vaud is organized to guarantee compulsory education through a cycle-based structure, designed to accompany the student from childhood until the completion of compulsory studies. The organization is based on precise age criteria for enrollment and follows a school calendar coordinated at the cantonal level, which defines lesson periods and holidays.
### The organization of school cycles Compulsory schooling in the Canton of Vaud is not a single block, but is divided into cycles that allow for gradual pedagogical progression. Each cycle has specific learning objectives and requires age requirements for access. Enrollment usually takes place based on the child's date of birth, ensuring that every student is placed in the class corresponding to their age group.
Languages of instruction represent a fundamental pillar of the system. Since Vaud is a French-speaking canton, French is the main medium of instruction, but the system provides for the introduction of other languages to prepare students for a national and international context. The management of these linguistic skills is integrated into the programs of each cycle, facilitating the integration of students coming from different linguistic regions of Switzerland or from abroad.
The transition between the various cycles is monitored to ensure that the student has acquired the necessary skills. This path culminates with the transition to upper secondary schools, where students are oriented toward academic or professional pathways based on their aptitudes and the results obtained during compulsory schooling. ### Practical implications for families For those settling in the Canton of Vaud, understanding how school cycles work is essential for planning their children's integration. Enrollment is not a single formal act, but a process that follows the child's growth stages. A parent arriving in the canton must verify which cycle their child falls into based on age, as access is strictly linked to this parameter.
The impact of the school calendar directly affects family and work organization. Since holiday and festive dates are established at the cantonal level, residents must coordinate their commitments with school closing periods. This is particularly relevant for those working in other cantons or having partners with different calendars.
### Transition and orientation scenarios Consider the hypothetical scenario of a student completing the compulsory education cycle. At this stage, the Canton of Vaud system provides a skills analysis for the transition to upper secondary schools. Depending on the results, the student may access general education paths or vocational paths. This orientation moment is critical, as it determines the young person's future professional or academic career.
Another scenario concerns linguistic integration. If a child is not fluent in French, the cantonal school system must manage their integration through linguistic support, given that teaching takes place predominantly in this language. The system's ability to adapt to different linguistic levels is a determining factor for initial academic success.
Organization into cycles also allows for greater pedagogical flexibility, enabling teachers to adapt teaching methods to the needs of the class group, while maintaining the standards required by the cantonal curriculum. This balance between regulatory rigor and didactic adaptation is what characterizes the educational approach in Vaud.

item.title: Vote 27 September: 63% no to neutrality
item.description: Gfs.bern survey: over 60% of voters intend to reject initiatives on neutrality and food security as of 27 September.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Over 60% of voters intend to reject both federal initiatives. - Sharp drop in support for neutrality and food security in early September. - Popular vote scheduled for September 27 in all Cantons.
## Key facts - Survey: according to the gfs.bern survey for SSR (SBC) - Referendum date: September 27 - Neutrality initiative: promoted by the Pro Suisse committee - Neutrality result: 63% opposed, 34% in favor - Food security result: 64% opposed, 33% in favor
A clear majority of the Swiss electorate is preparing to reject both texts submitted to the federal vote on September 27, according to the second survey conducted by the gfs.bern institute for the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation SBC. Indeed, over 60% of those interviewed declare their intention to vote no on both the neutrality proposal and the food security proposal. Support for both projects has visibly declined compared to the first survey conducted in early August. Had the consultation taken place in early September, 63% would have rejected the initiative titled 'Safeguarding Swiss neutrality', with a nine-point percentage jump in opposition. At the same time, the front of supporters has dropped by eight points, settling at 34%.
### The rejection of the Pro Suisse initiative The neutrality initiative, launched by the Pro Suisse committee, aims to directly enshrine the principle of a 'permanent and armed' Swiss neutrality in the Federal Constitution. However, the text faces strong cross-cutting opposition from almost all major Swiss political parties, from the Greens to the Liberals. Voters faithfully follow party lines: more than three-quarters of the supporters of these political forces declare a vote against. The rejection is particularly clear among Liberal Green voters, who reach 96% opposition. The Swiss People's Party (SVP) remains the only major party to formally support the proposal. Among its ranks, 77% of voters support the initiative, although the figure shows a nine-point percentage drop compared to the first survey. Independent voters have also changed their minds: 59% now reject the text, whereas a month earlier, more than half were in favor. Even among voters with a lower level of education, who were initially more inclined to vote yes, 54% now declare themselves opposed. The opposition to the initiative «For safe food» has developed with even greater rapidity on a federal scale. The text calls for incentives for plant-based food production to increase the country's food self-sufficiency rate, but it has been met with almost unanimous rejection. Currently, 64% of citizens oppose the measure, marking a 15-point increase in opponents, while support has dropped by 14 points to 33%. The Federal Parliament has rejected the proposal unanimously. Despite attempts by left-wing parties and the Liberal Greens to propose a counterproject, no alternative has found approval, leaving the text without institutional support.
On a geographical level, data collected by gfs.bern highlights a convergence between the different linguistic realities of the Confederation, an element closely monitored by federal offices such as UST/BFS and SECO in the analysis of civic sentiment. Regarding the neutrality initiative, in German-speaking Switzerland, 64% of respondents declare they want to vote no. In Romandy, opposition increases by 14 percentage points and reaches 63%. Italian-speaking Switzerland, on the other hand, shows a more balanced fracture: 48% supports the initiative promoted by Pro Suisse, compared to 47% opposed. For the food initiative, the no front dominates everywhere: opposition peaks at 66% in German-speaking Switzerland. Initially, Latin cantons had shown sympathy for the food text, but support has collapsed by 19 points in Romandy and by 16 points in Italian-speaking Switzerland. Rejection also crosses age groups: 58% of voters between 18 and 39 years old reject the food proposal, as do 59% of women. Among parties, while three-quarters of the Greens still vote in favor, support among socialists has slipped below 50%. Furthermore, the Liberal Greens have reversed their orientation: 52% now explicitly oppose the food measure.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). For residents called to the polls on September 27, the decisions on the two objects up for vote will have indirect repercussions on the overall framework of the Confederation, ranging from the debate on international relations led by the Federal Council to supply policies that may impact the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living). According to analyses by the gfs.bern institute, a reversal of the trend on the Pro Suisse initiative would require a massive mobilization of the SVP (UDC) electorate combined with a radical shift in the rest of the population, a scenario for which the institute detects no signs. Even on the food front, urban and suburban areas have aligned with rural zones, which have historically been skeptical of production constraints aimed at the plant sector.
### Voting methods and civic tools Those entitled to vote in Switzerland receive the official postal voting material directly at their home in the various Cantons several weeks before the set date. The procedure for participating in the democratic consultation follows precise steps: - Receipt of the official envelope containing the Federal Chancellery’s information sheets, voting certificates, and ballot papers. - Manual completion of the ballot, expressing ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ for each of the two federal questions. - Signing the voting certificate in the designated space to validate the vote. - Sending the stamped envelope by post before the deadline indicated by your municipality, or direct delivery to the municipal chancery of residence by the closing time of the polling stations on September 27.
